title: [spec-gap][R-19-036 + wiring] UX engines never started by any app; LED state never driven by device state; T1000-E has no led0 alias
description: spec/19-device-ux.md §10: the LED language states JOINING (0.5Hz/10%), MESSAGE_WAITING (0.25Hz/5%), FAULT (1Hz/50%) are never asserted anywhere — lichen_ux_led_state_set is called only from ux_button_zephyr.c (hold/SOS paths); zero callers map device state (RPL join status, msg-store unread, diag fault) to LED state (rg across lichen/: engine internals + tests only). Worse, lichen_ux_button_start/lichen_ux_led_start are called by NO app: lichen/apps/puck/src/main.c and gateway never start the engines, so the whole UX subsystem is dead at runtime on every target despite compiling (both default y via Kconfig). Also: T1000-E — a §2 tier-H headless target — has no led0/button0 alias in lichen/boards/seeed/t1000_e/t1000_e_nrf52840.dts, so lichen_hal_led_get fails there and the §10 language silently cannot drive its LED (backend degrades to no-op by design, ux_led_zephyr.c:47-53); its only LED work is the raw P0.24 boot blink in lichen/lib/native/native.c. Fix: start both engines from app boot (puck main.c), wire JOINING from RPL join state, MESSAGE_WAITING from message store, FAULT from lichen_diag, and add led0/button0 aliases to the T1000-E DTS. Test: extend host tests or add a native_sim scenario asserting state_set from simulated device events.
